en: O you who are a boat for crossing the waters of the solar lineage, who shine with the brilliance of the rising sun,
and who have dispelled the mass of darkness from the faces of the ten-headed Rāvaṇa— drive away the inner darkness within me!
O you whose excellent fame is celebrated for uprooting all the wicked with arrows drawn to the ear on your bow—dispel the web of my misdeeds that has churned the very core of my heart. || 2 ||
O Lord of my heart, having raised the moons of your toenails— which possess clusters of most beautiful rays— within my heart,
please indeed dispel the fever of my agitation as well as your own entire heat.

O you who are as beautiful as the petal of a blue lotus, O bestower of boons, O knower of Jānakī, I know you to be the Lord of all, the Lord of the world whose splendor shines even in the slightest degree. || 4 ||
O Beloved of Śaṅkara, grant that well-being which may quickly attain firm devotion and love for Your pair of feet, and long-lasting devotion toward the ocean of existence and its sorrows.
Even Vairājarājarāja became the king of the people of Susāketa;
for this was indeed the sole sport of the King of Monkeys (Rāma).
May this extensive hymn, composed for the great joy of the daughter of the mountain (Pārvatī), shine upon the lotus-like feet of that Rāma, who is like a bee. 7.
Thus ends the *Rāma-ṣaṭpadī*, composed by the illustrious Mathurānātha Śukla of the Mālavīya lineage.
